# Company 029 — Vertical Business OS Generator

**Company ID:** `company:future:029`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:029`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-029-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no vertical software launches.

## Business identity

Purpose: generate and operate configurable business operating systems for specific industries by combining shared CRM/scheduling/dispatch/quote/invoice/payment/document/compliance/analytics primitives with domain packs.

Problem: vertical businesses rely on fragmented generic tools or expensive custom software; each niche repeats the same foundational modules but needs domain terminology/workflows/integrations.

Value: reusable platform/factory that can produce differentiated vertical products without rebuilding common infrastructure.

## Product tree

Core Vertical OS Template; CRM/Leads; Customer/Property/Asset Records; Scheduling; Dispatch; Workforce/Technician; Quotes/Estimates; Contracts/Documents; Invoicing; Payments Integration; Inventory/Parts; Procurement; Work Orders; Field Service; Customer Portal; Communication; Forms/Photos/Media; Compliance/License Tracking; Recurring Service/Memberships; Routing/Maps; Time/Payroll Inputs; Reviews/Reputation; Marketing/Lead Intake; Analytics; Mobile/PWA; Offline Field Mode; API/SDK; White Label/OEM; Marketplace/Extensions; Vertical Pack Generator; Migration/Onboarding Tools.

## Vertical tree

Candidate verticals: garage doors, HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing, painting, landscaping/lawn, pest control, cleaning, junk removal, moving, handyman, remodeling, property maintenance, locksmith, appliance repair, pool/spa, auto service/detailing, towing, equipment service, commercial facilities, inspection, restoration, home healthcare administrative scheduling, pet services, beauty/wellness appointment businesses, tutoring/training, event services, specialty rentals, small logistics/courier, niche professional services.

Each vertical must be scored for distinct terminology, workflow, integrations, compliance, market competition, willingness to pay, data model differences and whether it deserves a standalone product/company rather than a pack.

## Brain / architecture

Brain learns domain terminology/workflow patterns, maps owner/business requirements to configurable modules, recommends process automation and generates domain pack specs. Deterministic business transactions own customer records, schedules, invoices/payments and permissions.

Architecture: modular SaaS kernel, plugin/module registry, domain-pack manifests, typed business entities, workflow engine, mobile/offline sync, integrations, billing/entitlement, reporting, event bus, policy. LLM for configuration, documentation, support and workflow design—not monetary record authority.

## Agents

Vertical Research Agent, Domain Ontology Agent, Product Pack Architect, Workflow Agent, Migration/Onboarding Agent, Integration Agent, Support Agent, QA Agent, Compliance Pack Agent, Analytics/Optimization Agent, Release Agent, Customer Success Agent.

## Deterministic services

Identity/orgs, CRM, scheduling/dispatch, quotes/invoices, payments refs, inventory, work orders, documents/media, messaging, notifications, search, reporting, offline sync, permissions, audit, API/webhooks, billing/entitlement, feature flags.

## Workflow

Select vertical → exhaustive domain research → define ontology/entities/workflows/compliance/integrations → assemble modules → configure domain pack → prototype/usability test → migrate sample data → test end-to-end → controlled beta only when separately authorized → measure gaps → iterate.

## Integrations / API / data

Accounting/payment, maps/routing, email/SMS/voice, calendars, suppliers/catalogs, payroll/time, CRM/marketing, forms/e-sign, review platforms, industry-specific equipment/regulator/vendor sources. Public API/webhooks, extension SDK, import/export.

Data moat: vertical workflow templates, domain ontologies, benchmark metrics, configuration patterns, migration mappings and product usability lessons. Customer business data isolated per product/company.

## Monetization / distribution

Per company/location/user/technician, modules/add-ons, transaction/communication usage, payments referral only where lawful, premium packs, API/OEM/white-label, marketplace commission, setup/migration, support. Distribution through vertical associations, suppliers, trade communities, app marketplaces, local-business ecosystems; no marketing now.

## Security/privacy/legal

Strong tenant isolation, payment/provider tokenization, customer PII, role permissions, mobile/offline security, audit, retention/export/delete, vertical compliance packs, protected financial/comms actions.

## Failure / edge cases

Vertical pack becomes too generic, offline conflicts, duplicate bookings, dispatch race, wrong tax/price, payment mismatch, contractor/employee permission differences, mobile device loss, supplier integration outage, multi-location complexity. Use modular contracts, conflict resolution, idempotency and vertical-specific tests.

## Scale / platform / spinoffs

Micro: one vertical product. ~$100K ARR: proven pack template. ~$1M: several verticals/shared kernel. ~$10M: marketplace/partner ecosystem. ~$100M+: vertical SaaS factory/platform if shared kernel remains truly reusable.

Potential independent vertical products go to spinoff registry; do not automatically add Company #101+.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** project type/domain-pack/module registries, extensible detail/workflow/data contracts, tenant/company isolation, billing/entitlement and integration abstractions.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center Foundry/project-type extensibility is directly relevant; reverse-map architecture carefully.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** customer tenant/auth/billing/deployment/support factories.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** actual vertical products/packs/integrations.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** marketplace and multi-vertical operational platform.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block

1. Product Tree: core template + CRM/schedule/dispatch/quotes/docs/invoice/payments/inventory/procurement/work orders/field/portal/comms/forms/compliance/recurring/routing/time/reviews/marketing/analytics/mobile/offline/API/OEM/marketplace/packs/migration.
2. Feature Tree: modular config/roles/import-export/search/report/automation/audit/security/billing/onboarding/offline/accessibility/localization/reliability.
3. Customer Tree: SMB field/service/appointment/professional businesses through multi-location enterprise/franchise/OEM.
4. Vertical Tree: exhaustive service/trade/appointment/professional niches scored for pack vs independent product.
5. Brain Tree: domain ontology/product/workflow/configuration/optimization reasoning; transactional truth deterministic.
6. Agent Tree: vertical research/ontology/product/workflow/migration/integration/support/QA/compliance/analytics/release/success.
7. Service Tree: auth/org/CRM/schedule/dispatch/financial refs/inventory/work/docs/comms/search/report/offline/permissions/API/billing.
8. Workflow Tree: research→pack spec→assemble→prototype→migrate→test→authorized beta→measure→iterate.
9. Integration Tree: accounting/payment/maps/comms/calendars/suppliers/payroll/marketing/e-sign/reviews/vertical sources.
10. Data Tree: customers/jobs/assets/work/orders/inventory/docs/financial refs/communications/metrics/domain config.
11. API Tree: business entities/workflows/webhooks/extensions/import-export.
12. Monetization Tree: org/location/user/technician/modules/usage/OEM/marketplace/setup/support.
13. Distribution Tree: associations/suppliers/trade channels/app marketplaces/local ecosystems.
14. Automation Tree: configuration/onboarding/scheduling/dispatch/reminders/docs/analytics/support; protected money/comms gated.
15. Moat Tree: shared kernel, vertical ontologies/workflows/integrations/migration maps/benchmarks.
16. Platform Tree: one vertical → vertical portfolio → extensible OS generator/marketplace.
17. Risk Tree: overgeneric product, tenant leakage, offline conflict, financial errors, vertical compliance gaps.
18. Scale Tree: one product→several packs→multi-vertical platform→global marketplace.
19. Spinoff Tree: independently valuable verticals recorded for later owner decision, not auto-added.
20. Command Center Dependencies: Foundry, project types, Brain/domain packs, Agent Factory, shared services, deployment/billing/support factories.
21. Design-Now: module/domain-pack/tenant/extensibility contracts.
22. Build-Now: Command Center project-type/Foundry extensibility strengthened after reverse-map.
23. Safe-to-Defer: actual customer OS products/vertical packs/billing/deployment/marketplace.
24. Autonomous Mature State: factory researches/specs/builds/tests/operates authorized vertical products using shared services; James chooses which verticals become businesses.

## Saturation result

Additional verticals remain pack/spinoff candidates. The core company is the generator/platform, so no automatic expansion beyond the canonical 100 occurs.

# Company 030 — Invoice / Payment Recovery AI

**Company ID:** `company:future:030`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:030`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-030-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no customer contact, payment-plan agreement, collections handoff or financial action.

## Business identity

Purpose: help businesses prioritize and recover overdue invoices through evidence-based account triage, respectful communication preparation, dispute tracking and cash forecasting.

Problem: AR teams manually chase invoices, miss disputes/promises, lack account prioritization and cannot distinguish process errors from real collection risk.

Value: organized receivables state, next-best-action recommendations, promise tracking, dispute resolution workflows and verified recovery attribution.

## Product tree

AR Aging Dashboard; Invoice/Account Priority Score; Payment Reminder Planner; Communication Drafts; Promise-to-Pay Tracker; Dispute Intake/Classification; Missing PO/Documentation Resolver; Payment Portal Links/Status; Account Health; Payment History; Cash Collection Forecast; Escalation Rules; Sales/Account-Manager Coordination; Partial Payment/Allocation Tracking; Payment Plan Workflow where lawful/authorized; Collection Handoff Package; Recovery Analytics; Root-Cause/Prevention Analytics; API/OEM; Vertical Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: invoice balance/due date/terms, aging buckets, customer/entity hierarchy, contact preferences, invoice delivery/open status, dispute reason, PO/reference, promise amount/date, payment/credit/refund, notes/evidence, risk/confidence, communication cadence, legal/compliance flags, escalation, forecast, audit.

Customers: SMB/midmarket/enterprise B2B, agencies, professional services, wholesalers/distributors, contractors, SaaS with invoices, logistics, manufacturers, staffing, property/service businesses.

Verticals: construction/subcontract, agencies/services, wholesale, logistics, staffing, SaaS/B2B subscriptions, manufacturing, property/vendor services. Debt-collection laws and customer type/jurisdiction matter.

## Brain / architecture

Brain analyzes account history, dispute cause, promises and likely recovery path; predicts cash timing and recommends next action/message. Deterministic ledger/reconciliation and policy own balances/cadence. It cannot threaten, misstate debt, agree legal terms or move money.

Architecture: AR/invoice ledger import, customer/entity graph, rules/state machine, communication consent/policy, forecast/risk model, document/evidence integration, LLM for cited communication drafts/dispute summaries, deterministic payment reconciliation.

## Agents

AR Triage Agent, Reminder Planner, Communication Draft Agent, Dispute Agent, Documentation Resolver, Promise Tracker, Account Health Agent, Cash Forecast Agent, Escalation Agent, Sales Coordination Agent, Handoff Package Agent, Recovery Attribution Agent, Root-Cause Agent, Compliance/Policy Agent.

## Deterministic services

Invoice/payment import; reconciliation; aging engine; promise scheduler; dispute state; communication queue/limits; document/evidence store; payment status connector; forecast calculator; escalation rules; audit; protected send/financial/legal gate.

## Workflow

Invoice becomes due → reconcile payment/credits → classify delinquency/dispute → prioritize account → check contact/legal policy → prepare reminder/action → authorized send/task → track reply/promise/dispute → resolve documentation → verify payment → update cash forecast/attribution → escalate or close.

## Integrations / API / data

Accounting/ERP, payment processors/banks (read/status), invoicing, CRM, email/SMS, customer portals, document/PO systems, sales/project systems, collections/legal handoff providers only when authorized. APIs for aging/accounts/disputes/promises/recommendations/forecast/recovery.

Data moat: account payment behavior, dispute taxonomy, action/outcome history, recovery timing models and root-cause patterns. Customer financial/communications data isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Invoices/accounts/AR volume, seats, subscription, verified-recovery share, enterprise/private, API/OEM, managed AR operations. Distribution through accounting/ERP/payment/CRM ecosystems, finance consultants/bookkeepers.

## Security/privacy/legal

Financial/customer data sensitive; no autonomous coercive communication; consent/channel/time rules; jurisdiction/debt-collection boundaries; protected payment plans/legal escalation/refunds/credits; no false balances; audit and evidence.

## Failure / edge cases

Payment received but not posted, credit memo pending, invoice disputed, wrong contact, invoice never delivered, duplicate invoice, customer insolvency, partial payment, multi-currency, tax withholding, promised payment missed, account under legal hold. Reconcile before outreach and surface unknown state.

## Scale/overlap

Small AR team → enterprise receivables operations. Overlap #10 subscription recovery, #61 autonomous collections, #85 revenue leakage, #86 payment reconciliation. #030 is pre-collections B2B invoice recovery.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** financial truth/reconciliation, communication/legal protected actions, evidence, scheduling, company/customer isolation.  
**BUILD NOW:** finance/comms/policy/event primitives after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** accounting/payment connector abstractions, consent/contact policy, financial audit.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** AR models/messages/customer portal/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** large enterprise portfolio forecasting/managed AR.

1. Product Tree: aging/priority/reminders/drafts/promises/disputes/docs/payment status/health/history/forecast/escalation/sales/partial/payment plans/handoff/analytics/prevention/API/packs.
2. Feature Tree: balances/terms/aging/hierarchy/preferences/delivery/disputes/PO/promises/payments/credits/evidence/risk/cadence/legal/forecast/audit.

4. Vertical Tree: construction, agencies, wholesale, logistics, staffing, SaaS, manufacturing, property services.
5. Brain Tree: account/dispute/recovery/cash reasoning and drafts; money/legal/comms actions gated.
6. Agent Tree: triage/reminder/draft/dispute/docs/promise/health/forecast/escalation/sales/handoff/attribution/root-cause/policy.
7. Service Tree: invoice/payment ingest/reconcile/aging/promises/dispute/comms/docs/payment connector/forecast/rules/audit.
8. Workflow Tree: due→reconcile→classify→prioritize→policy→action→track→resolve→verify payment→forecast/close.
9. Integration Tree: accounting/ERP/payment/invoice/CRM/comms/portal/docs/project/authorized collections.
10. Data Tree: invoices/payments/credits/accounts/disputes/promises/comms/evidence/forecasts/outcomes.
11. API Tree: aging/accounts/disputes/promises/recommendations/forecast/recovery.
12. Monetization Tree: invoices/accounts/AR/seats/recovery share/enterprise/private/API/OEM/managed.
13. Distribution Tree: accounting/ERP/payment/CRM/bookkeepers/finance consultants.
14. Automation Tree: reconciliation/aging/priority/reminders/tasks/forecast; sends/plans/legal escalation gated.
15. Moat Tree: payment/dispute/outcome history, recovery timing, root-cause corpus.
16. Platform Tree: AR assistant→recovery operations→receivables intelligence.
17. Risk Tree: wrong debt/contact, privacy, coercive messaging, legal boundaries, reconciliation errors.
18. Scale Tree: SMB→multi-entity enterprise→managed AR platform.
19. Spinoff Tree: adjacent #10/#61/#85/#86 already cover subscription/collections/leakage/reconciliation.

22. Build-Now: shared finance/comms/evidence hooks after reverse-map.
23. Safe-to-Defer: customer AR product/messages/models/portal/pricing.

# Company 031 — Business Form Automation Platform

**Company ID:** `company:future:031`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:031`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-031-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no form submission, signature, legal acceptance or external filing.

## Business identity

Purpose: turn repetitive forms into reusable, validated, source-linked profiles and workflow-ready submissions across web, PDF and document formats.

Problem: businesses repeatedly re-enter the same company/person/project information into changing forms and portals, causing errors, stale data and missed fields.

Value: canonical reusable data profiles, deterministic mapping/validation, document extraction, approval/signature routing and browser-assisted completion with full audit.

## Product tree

Reusable Business/Person Profiles; Field Dictionary & Semantic Mapping; PDF/Form Parser; Browser Form Mapper; Autofill Engine; Validation Rules; Conditional Question Logic; Attachment/Evidence Binder; Signature/Approval Routing; Version/Change Detection; Template Library; Form-to-Workflow Builder; Submission Readiness Checker; Browser Completion Assistant; Batch Form Generation; API/SDK/OEM; Vertical Form Packs; Enterprise Admin/Delegation; Private Runner.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: canonical fields, aliases, source/provenance, effective date, sensitive classification, required/optional fields, format/unit normalization, conditional sections, cross-field validation, attachment requirements, draft/save/resume, version diff, reviewer/approver, signature state, completion evidence, browser selector recovery, export/import, audit, accessibility/localization.

Customers: SMBs, enterprise ops, HR, procurement, grants/admin teams, vendor onboarding, credentialing, insurance/admin, construction, professional services, government contractors, developers embedding forms.

Verticals: vendor/customer onboarding, employment/admin, licensing/credentialing, grant administration, procurement, insurance/COI, construction/submittals, property/service applications, tax/admin forms, healthcare administrative intake, education/nonprofit. High-stakes legal/financial/government filing requires specialized review.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain understands form semantics, maps questions to canonical fields, identifies missing/conflicting answers, explains ambiguous wording and proposes reusable templates. Deterministic mapping/validation owns actual field values; protected submission/signature/attestation never occurs from model inference alone.

Architecture: canonical profile store, field ontology, form/document parser, OCR/layout, browser DOM mapper, rules/validation, attachment registry, workflow/approval engine, version hashes, LLM for semantic mapping/explanation, browser worker for authorized portals.

## Agent tree

Form Intake Agent, Field Mapping Agent, Profile Reconciliation Agent, Validation Agent, Attachment/Evidence Agent, Browser Mapping Agent, Version Drift Agent, Readiness Agent, Approval/Signature Coordinator, Vertical Pack Agent, QA Agent, Privacy Agent, Integration Agent.

## Deterministic services

Profile registry; schema/field dictionary; parser/OCR; mapping rules; value normalization; validation; attachment/hash store; template/version service; browser form state; approval/signature state; audit; protected submit gate; scheduler/reminders.

## Workflow

Ingest form → parse/version → map fields to canonical profile → identify missing/conflict → retrieve approved evidence → validate → human/owner review where required → generate/fill draft → protected signature/submit boundary → capture receipt/status → update reusable mappings only from verified outcomes.

## Integrations / API / data

Document/PDF tools, browsers, e-sign, cloud storage, CRM/HRIS/procurement, credential/vendor systems, government/public portals where authorized, email, workflow/task systems. APIs for forms/schema/profile/mapping/validation/readiness/draft/status.

Data moat: field ontology, mapping templates, portal/form version history, validation/error corpus and reusable vertical packs; customer form contents remain isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Forms/submissions/pages, profiles, seats, browser minutes, vertical packs, enterprise/private, API/OEM, managed setup. Distribution through onboarding/procurement/credentialing/HR/e-sign/document ecosystems and integrators.

## Security/privacy/legal

Forms can contain PII, tax, banking, identity and legal attestations. Encrypt/scoped access, secret/credential refs, no model training by default, protected signature/attestation/submission, source provenance, retention/export/delete, no bypass of portal controls.

## Failure / edge cases

Question wording changes, ambiguous aliases, stale profile value, conditional page hidden, CAPTCHA/user-presence requirement, upload size/type, signature authority, conflicting attachments, legal attestation, browser DOM drift. Fail closed on ambiguity and preserve exact submitted snapshot.

## Scale/platform/overlap

Single forms → recurring enterprise form library → cross-portal form infrastructure. Overlap #9 document-to-workflow, #38 grant management, #62 credentialing, #63 vendor onboarding, #42 browser workers. #031 focuses on reusable form completion/mapping.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** canonical owner/company profile refs, field provenance, untrusted document/browser boundary, protected submit/signature action, version snapshots.  
**BUILD NOW:** shared owner-input/profile and browser/document contracts after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** secure profile vault interface, browser-worker isolation, approval/signature abstractions.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** form library/portal mappings/customer product.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** large cross-portal mapping network.

# Company 032 — AI Procurement Assistant

**Company ID:** `company:future:032`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:032`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-032-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no purchases, supplier commitments, contracts, payments or external negotiation.

## Business identity

Purpose: help organizations define purchase requirements, compare suppliers/quotes/contracts, enforce budgets/approvals and prepare procurement decisions.

Problem: purchasing requests are fragmented, specifications unclear, quote comparison manual, vendor data inconsistent and approvals disconnected from spend policy.

Value: structured sourcing packets, normalized quote analysis, supplier/risk context, savings scenarios and traceable approvals.

## Product tree

Purchase Request Intake; Requirement/Specification Builder; Catalog Search/Match; Supplier Registry; Quote/RFQ Comparison; Total-Cost-of-Ownership Analyzer; Contract/Terms Comparison; Budget/Cost-Center Check; Approval Routing; Supplier Scoring; Negotiation Prep; Purchase Recommendation; PO Draft/ERP Handoff; Procurement Calendar/Renewals; Spend Analytics; Preferred Supplier/Item Catalog; Procurement Policy Engine; API/OEM; Vertical Packs; Enterprise/Private Deployment.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: requesters, cost centers, quantities, specs, must/should criteria, approved vendors, quote line normalization, shipping/tax/fees, delivery lead time, warranty/support, terms, risk/compliance, scoring weights, alternatives, approvals, budget availability, split orders, exceptions, evidence, audit, accessible/localized workflows.

Customers: SMB/midmarket/enterprise procurement, finance, IT, operations, facilities, manufacturing, construction, hospitality, nonprofits/education, SaaS/tech purchasing, agencies, multi-location organizations.

Verticals: IT/SaaS, MRO/industrial, construction/materials, office/facilities, hospitality/food-service supplies, logistics, professional services, marketing procurement, healthcare administrative supplies, education/nonprofit. Regulated procurement/public-sector rules require specialized packs and human review.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain translates business need into requirements, compares quote/contract tradeoffs, suggests alternatives and negotiation points, predicts supplier/lead-time/cost risk and explains recommendations. Deterministic policy/budget/vendor eligibility owns approval gates. It cannot place orders, accept contracts or move funds without protected authorization.

Architecture: supplier/item/catalog registry, quote/document parser, normalization/TCO calculator, rules/policy engine, vendor-risk integration, budget/finance reference, optimization/constraint solver, LLM for requirements/terms comparison with citations, workflow/approval state.

## Agent tree

Requirement Agent, Catalog/Alternative Agent, Supplier Analyst, Quote Normalization Agent, TCO Agent, Contract Comparison Agent, Budget/Policy Agent, Vendor-Risk Liaison, Negotiation Prep Agent, Approval Coordinator, PO Draft Agent, Spend Analyst, Procurement QA Agent, Integration Agent.

## Deterministic services

Request registry; supplier/item master; quote parser; unit/currency normalization; TCO calculator; budget checker; approval workflow; policy engine; vendor eligibility; scoring/constraint optimizer; PO draft service; audit; protected purchase/contract gate; reconciliation hooks.

## Workflow

Request → clarify requirements → identify approved/eligible sources → collect authorized quotes → normalize/TCO/risk → score alternatives → budget/policy check → recommendation → approval → protected PO/purchase/contract action in external system → verify receipt/price → record outcome/supplier performance.

## Integrations / API / data

ERP/procurement, accounting/budget, vendor catalogs, contract systems, vendor risk, inventory, AP, expense/cards, supplier portals, e-sign, logistics/receiving. APIs for requests/requirements/suppliers/quotes/comparisons/recommendations/approvals.

Data moat: normalized item/supplier/quote graph, TCO history, supplier performance, negotiated-term patterns, requirement templates and verified savings outcomes; customer spend isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Seats, spend under management, requests/quotes, supplier count, enterprise/private, API/OEM, premium benchmarks/managed procurement, verified-savings share where transparent. Distribution through ERP/accounting/procurement marketplaces, consultants/integrators, vertical supplier ecosystems.

## Security/legal/privacy

Confidential pricing/contracts/budgets; supplier fairness; no collusion; protected purchase/contracts; separation of duties; audit; no hidden kickback ranking; regional procurement/public contracting rules; financial controls.

## Failure / edge cases

Non-comparable quotes, hidden shipping/terms, supplier capacity change, counterfeit/unauthorized seller, budget race, currency volatility, sole-source exception, emergency purchase, wrong quantity/unit, tax handling, contract conflict, late delivery. Require normalized evidence and explicit exceptions.

## Scale / overlap

Team purchasing → enterprise sourcing/procurement intelligence. Overlap #17 SaaS spend, #23 contracts, #24 vendor risk, #48 AP verification, #63 onboarding. #032 owns requirement-to-purchase-decision workflow.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** protected purchasing/contract actions, finance/cost-center refs, vendor identity, evidence/TCO/approval interfaces.  
**BUILD NOW:** generic policy/finance/vendor/approval contracts after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** company budget/resource governor, vendor registry/isolation, purchase authorization interface.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** supplier catalogs/quote models/customer portal/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** large benchmark/supplier network and autonomous preapproved purchasing.
